question.problem:
Sam wanted to estimate the rate of weight growth of his new puppy. He took note of its weight every week, for $7$ weeks. The results are shown in the table below, where $W(t)$ is the puppy's weight (measured in pounds) after $t$ weeks from birth.

| **$t$** | $8$ | $9$ | $10$ | $11$ | $12$ | $13$ | $14$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $W(t)$ | $9$ | $10.1$ | $11.3$ | $12.4$ | $13.5$ | $14.6$ | $15.8$ |

$$

$$

Approximate the puppy's rate of weight growth $12$ weeks after birth using a central difference approximation with step size $h=1.$

current_example.problem:
A car engine is being heated from a temperature of about $-10^{\circ}.$ The temperature of the engine after $t$ minutes is given by $T(t).$  The graph of $T(t)$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14194746/assets/fe78a78911e2df9cdb488ec57b0e0a34bb56e18b57303d895dc8013b64a4afc3.png)

Approximate the rate at which the temperature of the engine increases when $t = 3$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=1.$
current_example.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
T'(t) \approx \dfrac{T(t+h) - T(t-h)}{2h},
$$

 

at the time $t=3$ with step size $h=1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(3) & ≈\frac{T(3+1)-T(3-1)}{2(1)} \\  & =\frac{T(4)-T(2)}{2} \\  & =\frac{60-30}{2} \\  & =\frac{30}{2} \\  & =15.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the rate of temperature increase is approximately $15^{\circ}$ per minute.
